subject: updateNumericInput takes one cycle to update, where updateSliderInput takes two!!!

messages.author: 3a28b296167ce88d
messages.subject: updateNumericInput takes one cycle to update, where updateSliderInput takes two!!!
parts:
Hi Everyone,

 

I have been dealing with a really frustrating issue that I cannot seem to resolve.  I have read everything I could find on the topic – including these boards – and there does not seem to be any good explanations as to what is happening underneath the R code in order to help inform where I should go from here. I have limited javascript knowledge, so I am aware the answers might be staring me in the face.

 

I have ten pairs of dual reactive (or bi-directional) widgets, and the pairs consist of a numeric and slider field that reflects the same value.  My application has a rather complex system that updates either of the two necessary widgets to whatever value was most recently modified in the user interface.  This update occurs after a preset period has passed of no subsequent user modifications.  The dependent reactive functions, which render my plots, are triggered by the user updated numeric fields’ values, not the sliders.  The actual widget update commands are carried out within a function inside of an observe block.

 

Side note from http://www.inside-r.org/packages/cran/shiny/docs/updateNumericInput:  For update functions, “The messages are collected and sent after all the observers (including outputs) have finished running.”  Is there a name for this, because it is not called “console flush?”  For the purposes of this thread, I am going to call it, a “cycle”; therefore a “cycle” will be defined as when server decides all of its reactions and observers are complete, and it is time to send information back to the UI.  I would love to know the true technical name for this.

 

My big issue is just after a “cycle” when both the updateNumericInput() and updateSliderInput() functions are executed with the same value, and all the graphs have been updated on the UI.  The next cycle’s initial observe function (i.e. the observe function that triggers all other reactions), takes in both the input$numtxt and input$slider values, however, the numtxt is the correct (just updated) value, and the slider is the previous (not updated) value.  To reiterate, this happens even if both fields received an update (e.g. due to the numtxt field being out of bounds, or NA). 

 

The strange thing is, after the subsequent cycle finishes running, the next cycle (after the previous broken cycle) takes in the correct value regardless if the slider was updated a second time due to a complete rerun.  I thought for a moment that there was an issue with a delay.  That is, that it took a second for the UI to be ready to tell the server its value was updated, but I ruled that out.  I am currently using a workaround where the initial observe function executes one extra time after every completed cycle making absolutely no invalidations or resumes() in its descendants.  This brief extra cycle seems to be enough for the input$slider value to be the correct updated value.  Just to be thorough I used the bug tracker feature to watch the exact values going to into the updateSliderInput() function, and everything exactly as it should, and is exactly like the values going into the updateNumericInput() function.

 

Does anyone have any insights as to what is happening here, where I might have gone wrong, and/or what I should read to get a great understanding?  One of the things I wanted to figure out was exactly what information the server is sending out in the output.  I tried for some time to get to get a profile of the input and output information and print([info]) ; flush.console() it so I can see it pre-cycle.  It seems the information entering the session by way of the session$sendInputMessage() function is not readable, and if it is I would love to know how.

 

Any help would be greatly appreciated!

 

Thanks,

Reino

 

P.S. If I get some support through these boards, I will be glad to keep this thread up-to-date with what I learn on the topic.

P.P.S. I never using a "." character in any of my variable names.

Here is an example:

ui.R
library(shiny)
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("Example"),
  sidebarPanel(
    numericInput("numtxt", label = h6("numtxt"),
                 min = 0, max = 100, step = 10, value = 50),
   
    sliderInput("slider", label = h6("slider"),
                min = 1, max = 100, value = 100)
  ),
  mainPanel(
    plotOutput("distPlot")
  )
))

server.R
library(shiny)
shinyServer(function(session, input, output) {
  r_val <- reactiveValues()
  r_val[['count']] <- 0
  line_number <<- 0
  lnum <- function(){line_number <<- line_number + 1 ; paste0(line_number," ")}
  fixer_func <- function(num, slr){
    print(paste0(lnum(),"numtxt is being updated from: ", num, " to ", 50)) ; flush.console()
    updateNumericInput(session, inputId = "numtxt", value = 50)
    print(paste0(lnum(),"slider is being updated from: ", slr, " to ", 50)) ; flush.console()
    updateSliderInput(session,  inputId = "slider", value = 50)
  }
  session$onFlush(function(){print(paste0(lnum(),"#### Pre flush ####")) ; flush.console()})
  session$onFlushed(function(){print(paste0(lnum(),"#### Post flush ####")) ; flush.console()})
  observe({
    print(paste0(lnum(),"## Observe Executed ##")) ; flush.console()
    print(paste0(lnum(),"# Current Cycle Number = ", isolate(r_val[['count']]), " #"))
    numtxt <- input$numtxt
    slider <- input$slider
    print(paste0(lnum(),"# numtxt = ", numtxt, " slider = ", slider, " #")) ; flush.console()
    if( numtxt >= 50 & slider >= 50 ){
      isolate(r_val[['count']] <- r_val[['count']] + 1)
    } else{
      fixer_func(numtxt, slider)
    }
  })
  for_plots <- reactive({
    print(paste0(lnum(),"## reactive Executed ##")) ; flush.console()
    r_val[['count']]
   
    isolate(value <- input$numtxt + input$slider)
    print(paste0(lnum(),"# value: ", value, " #")) ; flush.console()
    return(value)
  })
  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
    print(paste0(lnum(),"## renderPlot Executed ##")) ; flush.console()
    data <- for_plots()
    plot(rnorm(data), rnorm(data))
  })
})

In order to observe the behavior I am referring to in my original post just, just click on the 50 in the "numtxt" numeric entry box, and delete just the zero. The app should run immediately and spit out in the console this text:

Listening on http://XXX.X.X.X:XXXX
[1] "1 ## Observe Executed ##"
[1] "2 # Current Cycle Number = 0 #"
[1] "3 # numtxt = 50 slider = 100 #"
[1] "4 ## renderPlot Executed ##"
[1] "5 ## reactive Executed ##"
[1] "6 # value: 150 #"
[1] "7 #### Pre flush ####"
[1] "8 #### Post flush ####"
[1] "9 ## Observe Executed ##"
[1] "10 # Current Cycle Number = 1 #"
[1] "11 # numtxt = 5 slider = 100 #"
[1] "12 numtxt is being updated from: 5 to 50"
[1] "13 slider is being updated from: 100 to 50"
[1] "14 ## Observe Executed ##"
[1] "15 # Current Cycle Number = 1 #"
[1] "16 # numtxt = 50 slider = 100 #"
[1] "17 ## renderPlot Executed ##"
[1] "18 ## reactive Executed ##"
[1] "19 # value: 150 #"
[1] "20 ## Observe Executed ##"
[1] "21 # Current Cycle Number = 2 #"
[1] "22 # numtxt = 50 slider = 50 #"
[1] "23 ## renderPlot Executed ##"
[1] "24 ## reactive Executed ##"
[1] "25 # value: 100 #"


The issue I am having is that on line 13 "slider is being updated from: 100 to 50." I have looked at this in the debugger; the slider really IS being updated to 50, however, on line 16 "# numtxt = 50 slider = 100 #", you can see that the slider is still being taken in as 100, and has not been updated. Additionally, you can see that it runs twice from lines 14 to 16, before it meets the criteria to update the plot. This should also be counted as two cycles, instead of one. It seems two when two updates take place, the observe function schedules two invalidations back to back, and one one changes at a time.

What I would love to figure out how to stop it from reexecuting like on line 20.

messages.subject: Re: updateNumericInput takes one cycle to update, where updateSliderInput takes two!!!
parts:
Thanks for the info, that made it a piece of cake to diagnose and fix!

The issue is specific to the sliderInput. The sliderInput uses a 250 millisecond debounce for performance/responsiveness reasons. So the numericInput sends its new value immediately while the sliderInput waits 250ms to make sure you're not going to change the value some more.

I've got an experimental fix that you can try with:

devtools::install_github("rstudio/shiny@joe/bugfix/slider-delay")

Don't forget to restart R after installing.

Also, in the future, you might find options(shiny.trace=TRUE) to be helpful; set it before running your Shiny app and Shiny will dump the messages it sends and receives to the R console. In this case I could clearly see that the updated values from each of the input controls were coming in two different messages, and with the fix they are coalesced into one.
